title: Determination 2023/017: The proposed issue of a notice to fix regarding the change of use of motel units
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Rotorua Lakes Council as territorial authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Act 2004 ss 114-115 and Change of Use Regulations (use groups SA and SR); Building Code clauses G3 and H1.3.4(c) are discussed. The Building Code edition is not stated in the text read.

facts.text: A motel in Rotorua was previously used as tourist accommodation and was later used for emergency housing.
The question is whether the use group changed from sleeping accommodation (SA) to sleeping residential (SR) and, if so, whether that created additional or more onerous Building Code requirements.
The authority's submission listed the fire-safety requirements under clause C for SR as additional or more onerous requirements.
The authority submitted that there had been at least eight fires in motels used as emergency housing in the past two years in Rotorua.

For a change not incorporating household units, compliance is measured against a qualified set of Building Code requirements: means of escape from fire, protection of other property, sanitary facilities, structural performance, fire-rating performance, and access for disabled people where section 118 applies.
On or about 24 January 2022 the authority proposed to issue a notice to fix under section 164 to the landlord.

limitations: Change-of-use classification is the main ground. The fire and escape content is in the statutory test and the parties' submissions.
The council's fire-incident statistic is a submission, not a finding in this determination.
The decision (p.37 §8.1) is in the same PDF as the facts. Outcome leakage is true unless redacted.
Owner and operator names are left out of the prompt.
Applies to the New Zealand Building Act and Building Code only. No Alberta applicability is asserted.
